messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, tumhare gaanv mein agar do padosiyon mein zameen ko lekar jhagda ho jaaye aur Panchayat ka faisla dono ko manzoor na ho, to wo log aage kahan jaate hain?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir wo log court jaate hain na — pehle chhoti court, phir bade court mein appeal karte hain agar wahan bhi santusht na hon.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Aur agar sabse badi State ki court ka faisla bhi kisi ko manzoor na ho, to appeal ka aakhri, sabse upar wala pada kya hai? Wahi jahan se ab koi aur upar appeal nahi ho sakti?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Wo to Supreme Court hoga sir! Sabse upar, jiske baad koi aur court nahi hoti.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi Raju! Supreme Court of India desh ki 'Apex Court' hai — matlab poore judicial system ke piramid ka sabse upar wala point. Iske faisle ke baad koi aur judicial forum nahi hota — ye final hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! To Supreme Court ka faisla ek dum final hota hai? Koi bhi usse ooncha nahi hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! Aur ek zaroori baat — Supreme Court sirf appeal sunne wali court nahi hai, ye 'Constitution ka Guardian' bhi hai — matlab Constitution ki raksha karna, Fundamental Rights ki suraksha karna, aur poore desh mein kanoon ki ek samaan vyakhya (uniform interpretation) sunishchit karna bhi iska kaam hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Guardian of Constitution! Ye to bahut bada role hai sir. Ye sab kahan likha hai Constitution mein?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Supreme Court se related poora vidhan Constitution ke Part V (Union) mein, Chapter IV mein, Article 124 se lekar Article 147 tak diya gaya hai. Isme judges ki niyukti, unki qualification, jurisdiction — sab kuch cover hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 124 se 147 — itna lamba! Sir, Supreme Court kab banaya gaya tha? Independence ke turant baad?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut achha sawaal! Supreme Court of India ka udghatan (inauguration) 28 January 1950 ko hua — Constitution lagu hone ke sirf 2 din baad (26 January 1950 se). Isse pehle 'Federal Court of India' (1937-1950) tha, jise Supreme Court ne replace kiya.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Federal Court pehle tha, phir Supreme Court aaya. 28 January — ye date yaad rakhni hogi sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek aur important fact — Article 130 kehta hai ki Supreme Court ki 'seat' (sthaan) Delhi mein hogi. Lekin ek twist hai — Chief Justice, President ki manzoori se, Supreme Court ki koi bhi sitting Delhi ke alaawa kisi aur jagah bhi kar sakte hain!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab Supreme Court Delhi ke alawa kisi aur city mein bhi baith sakta hai? Kya ye kabhi hua hai practically?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Constitutionally possible hai, par practically abhi tak aisa nahi hua hai. Ye ek proposed 'Bench outside Delhi' wala reform proposal bhi hai jo discuss hota rehta hai — access to justice ke liye. Par abhi tak Supreme Court sirf Delhi mein hi baithta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, theoretically possible hai par practically nahi hua — ye trap ban sakta hai exam mein. Ab batao sir, Supreme Court mein judges kitne hote hain?

quiz_payload.explanation: Supreme Court se related provisions Article 124 se 147 tak (Part V, Chapter IV) diye gaye hain. Article 214-231 High Courts se, 148-151 CAG se, aur 76-78 Attorney General/Council of Ministers se sambandhit hain.

quiz_payload.explanation: Supreme Court of India ka udghatan 28 January 1950 ko hua, Constitution lagu hone ke 2 din baad. Isse pehle 'Federal Court of India' (1937-1950) desh ki apex judicial body thi.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, socho — jab Supreme Court 1950 mein shuru hua, tab kya usme aaj jitne hi judges the, ya kam the?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir shuruaat mein kam log honge, kyunki desh chhota shuru hua hoga, cases bhi kam hongi na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi soch! 1950 mein Supreme Court mein sirf 1 Chief Justice aur 7 other judges the — total 8 judges. Original Article 124(1) mein yehi likha tha. Lekin jaise-jaise cases badhti gayi, Parliament ne kanoon banakar ye number badhaaya.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! To ye number fixed nahi hai, Parliament badal sakti hai? Aaj kitne judges hain sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakda! Article 124(1) khud kehta hai ki judges ki sankhya Parliament kanoon banakar badal sakti hai. 2019 mein Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act se ye sankhya badhakar 34 kar di gayi — 1 Chief Justice of India (CJI) + 33 other judges.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 34! Pehle 8 the, ab 34 ho gaye. Ye to bahut badh gaya sir. Sabse recent kab badha tha?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 2019 mein hi last badhotri hui — usse pehle 2009 mein 31 tak badhaya gaya tha, phir 2019 mein 34 kiya gaya. Ye timeline yaad rakho: 1950 mein 8, phir bade steps mein 31 (2009), phir 34 (2019).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 8 se 31, phir 34 — ye numbers yaad rakhne honge. Ab batao sir, judges ki niyukti kaun karta hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Article 124(2) ke anusar SC ke judges ko 'President' niyukt karte hain. Lekin sirf naam se President appoint nahi karte — ek poori 'consultation process' follow hoti hai. CJI ki niyukti ke liye President 'such judges' se consult karte hain jinhe wo zaroori samjhein.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Consultation matlab? President kisi se salaah lete hain phir appoint karte hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Aur ye consultation process hi aage chalkar bahut bada issue bana — kyunki Constitution mein 'consultation' likha tha, lekin iska matlab kya hoga — 'sirf salaah lena' ya 'salaah maanna zaroori hai' — iske baare mein Supreme Court ke khud kai landmark judgements aaye. Isi se 'Collegium System' ka janam hua, jo hum Module 9 mein detail se padhenge.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, ye 'Collegium System' wala part baad mein aayega — abhi bas itna samajh liya ki President appoint karte hain with consultation.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab do special provisions yaad karo jo bahut kam log jaante hain — Article 127 kehta hai ki agar SC mein kaam ke liye quorum poora karne ke liye judges kam pad jaayein, to CJI, President ki manzoori se, 'ad hoc judge' — matlab kisi High Court ke qualified judge ko — temporarily bula sakte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! High Court ka judge temporary Supreme Court mein aa sakta hai? Interesting hai ye!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul! Aur Article 128 mein ek aur interesting provision hai — CJI, President ki manzoori se, kisi retired SC judge ya retired High Court judge (jo SC judge banne yogya ho) ko bhi request kar sakte hain SC mein temporarily sitting karne ke liye — inhe 'retired judges sitting as SC judges' kaha jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Wow, matlab retire ho chuke judge bhi wapas aa sakte hain kaam karne? Ye to bahut flexible system hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab batao Raju — SC judge banne ke liye kya-kya chahiye? Article 124(3) mein 3 raaste (paths) diye gaye hain jinse koi vyakti SC judge ban sakta hai. Pehla — Indian citizen hona zaroori hai, ye sabke liye common hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, aur baaki do raaste kya hain sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Doosra raasta — koi vyakti kam se kam 5 saal tak High Court judge raha ho (ek ya adhik High Courts mein), ya teesra raasta — koi vyakti kam se kam 10 saal tak High Court mein advocate raha ho (ek ya adhik High Courts mein).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 5 saal judge, ya 10 saal advocate. Aur ek teesra bhi bola tha aapne — wo kya hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut achha yaad rakha! Teesra raasta hai — 'Distinguished Jurist' — matlab koi bahut vidwan (learned) legal scholar, jise President ki nazar mein kanoon ka bahut gehra gyaan ho. Iske liye koi minimum years ki requirement nahi likhi hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Distinguished jurist? Matlab koi law professor bhi ban sakta hai SC judge, bina judge ya advocate rahe bhi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Theoretically haan, Constitution mein ye option hai. Lekin practically, aaj tak koi bhi 'Distinguished Jurist' ke roop mein directly SC judge nahi bana hai — ye ek unused provision hai. Ye BPSC ka interesting trap hai — 'kya kisi Distinguished Jurist ko SC judge banaya gaya hai?' Jawab — Constitutional provision hai, par practically use nahi hua.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Ye to bahut sneaky trap hai — theory mein possible, practically kabhi hua nahi. Yaad rakhunga sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ek aur bahut important trap — SC judge banne ke liye Constitution mein koi MINIMUM AGE define NAHI ki gayi hai! Sirf High Court judge ke 5 saal ya advocate ke 10 saal ki 'experience' requirement hai, age directly nahi.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Koi minimum age nahi?? To phir retirement age hogi na kम se kam?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut sahi doubt! Haan, retirement age hai — Article 124(2) ke proviso ke anusar SC judge 65 saal ki umra tak kaam karte hain, phir retire ho jaate hain. Ye High Court judges se alag hai jo 62 saal mein retire hote hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: SC judge 65 par, HC judge 62 par! Ye fark yaad rakhna zaroori hai — HC se kam retirement age hai to SC judge zyada der tak kaam kar sakte hain.

quiz_payload.question: Article 124(3) ke anusar SC judge banne ke liye nimnlikhit mein se kaunsa raasta VALID NAHI hai?

options.text: Kam se kam 5 saal High Court judge rahe hon
Kam se kam 10 saal High Court advocate rahe hon

Kam se kam 15 saal Lok Sabha ke Member of Parliament rahe hon

quiz_payload.explanation: MP hone ka SC judge banne se koi sambandh nahi hai — ye kabhi bhi valid path nahi raha. Valid paths hain: 5 saal HC judge, 10 saal HC advocate, ya Distinguished Jurist.

quiz_payload.question: SC judges kis umra mein retire hote hain, aur ye High Court judges se kaise alag hai?

options.text: SC judge 62 saal, HC judge 65 saal
SC judge 65 saal, HC judge 62 saal
Dono 65 saal mein retire hote hain
Dono 60 saal mein retire hote hain

quiz_payload.explanation: SC judges 65 saal ki umra mein retire hote hain (Article 124(2) proviso), jabki High Court judges 62 saal mein retire hote hain (Article 217) — ye zyada common exam trap hai.

Sahi kathan chuniye:

options.text: Kewal Kathan 1 sahi hai

quiz_payload.explanation: Dono kathan sahi hain — Constitution mein SC judge ke liye koi minimum age nahi hai, aur 'Distinguished Jurist' wala provision aaj tak practically use nahi hua hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, ab SC judge ki shapath (oath) ke baare mein — Article 124(6) ke anusar SC judge ko shapath kaun dilaata hai, guess karo?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: President honge sir, jaise VP aur CAG ko bhi President hi shapath dilaate hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! President (ya President dwara niyukt koi vyakti) SC judges ko shapath dilaate hain. Shapath mein judge ye kehta hai ki wo Constitution ke prati sachchi nishtha rakhega, apne kartavya bina dar ya prem-bhaav (fear or favour) ke, bina anurag ya dwesh (affection or ill-will) ke nibhayega, aur Constitution ki raksha karega.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 'Bina dar, bina prem-bhaav' — ye important line hai sir! Ye judicial independence ka core spirit lagta hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab salary ki baat karte hain — SC judges ki salary Second Schedule mein di gayi hai aur Parliament kanoon se ise revise kar sakti hai. Current mein CJI ki salary Rs 2,80,000 prati mah aur other SC judges ki salary Rs 2,50,000 prati mah hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: CJI 2.8 lakh, judges 2.5 lakh. Aur ye salary bhi kya kabhi ghata sakte hain sarkar?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut zaroori sawaal! Article 125(2) ke proviso mein kaha gaya hai ki judge ke 'privileges, allowances, aur pension rights' unke niyukti ke baad, unke nuksaan mein nahi badle ja sakte — SAAMANYA sthiti mein. Lekin ek exception hai — agar 'Financial Emergency' (Article 360) lagu ho, tab reduction ho sakta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Normal mein kabhi salary kam nahi hogi, par Financial Emergency mein ho sakti hai. Ye exception yaad rakhunga sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab sabse important topic — SC judge ko hataya kaise jaata hai? Article 124(4) ke anusar isse 'removal' kaha jaata hai, jise 'impeachment' bhi bola jaata hai. Ye process President karte hain, lekin sirf Parliament ke resolution ke baad.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Impeachment! Ye to President wala process hai na sir? SC judge ka bhi wahi hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut achha connect! Similar hai, par exact same nahi. SC judge ko hataane ke liye — 1) dono sadan mein resolution laaya jaata hai, 2) special majority chahiye — total membership ka majority + present-voting ka 2/3rd, 3) ground hona chahiye 'proved misbehaviour ya incapacity', aur 4) SAME session mein dono sadan mein resolution paas hona zaroori hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Same session mein dono sadan! Ye extra condition hai jo President ke impeachment mein nahi thi na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi observation! Aur ek zaroori procedural detail — Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 ke anusar, jab removal ka motion Parliament mein lagaya jaata hai, to pehle ek 3-member committee banti hai (ek SC judge, ek HC Chief Justice, aur ek distinguished jurist) jo charges ki janch karti hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab pehle ek committee investigate karti hai, tab jaake Parliament mein vote hota hai? Ye ek extra safeguard hai!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Agar committee 'guilty' finding de, tabhi Parliament vote karti hai. Isi wajah se aaj tak koi bhi SC judge is process se successfully hataya nahi ja saka hai — ye itni tough hai ki koi bhi motion 2/3rd majority tak nahi pahuncha.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Koi bhi judge aaj tak hata nahi paaye?? Ye to bahut hi strong protection hai! India mein aisa koi case try to hua hoga na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan Raju, ek famous case hai — Justice V. Ramaswami (1993) — jinke khilaf motion Lok Sabha mein aaya tha corruption charges par. Committee ne unhe guilty bhi paya, lekin voting ke waqt Congress party ne abstain (vote nahi) kiya, isliye motion required 2/3rd majority tak nahi pahuncha aur wo bach gaye.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Committee ne guilty kaha lekin phir bhi bach gaye kyunki majority nahi mili. Ye to bahut interesting real case hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul, ye PYQ mein aa chuka hai! Yaad rakho — abhi tak koi bhi SC ya HC judge Parliament dwara successfully removed nahi hua hai. Kuch judges ne process shuru hone se pehle hi resign kar diya, jaise Justice Soumitra Sen (Calcutta HC, 2011).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Resign karke bach gaye. Ye poora removal wala topic bahut detailed hai, ab quiz karte hain sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, ab ek comprehensive picture banate hain — kyun Supreme Court itna independent (swatantra) hai? Humne kai safeguards abhi tak dekhe hain — tough removal, protected salary. Ab kuch aur bhi dekhte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Haan sir, ye important lag raha hai — kyunki independent judiciary hi to fair faisla de sakti hai na?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi soch! Ek aur zaroori safeguard — SC judge ka conduct (kaam-kaaj) Parliament ya State Legislature mein discuss NAHI kiya ja sakta, EXCEPT jab removal ka motion process chal raha ho (Article 121 aur 211).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Matlab MP log Parliament mein baithke judge ki criticize nahi kar sakte, sirf removal ke process mein hi baat ho sakti hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye Article 121/211 ek bahut powerful protection hai. Ab ek aur safeguard — SC ke administrative staff (karmachari) ki niyukti CJI khud karte hain (ya CJI ke authorize kiye kisi aur judge/officer), Parliament ki koi seedhi dakhal-andaazi nahi hoti (Article 146).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, apna staff bhi khud hi choose karte hain! Aur SC ki practice-procedure kaun tय karta hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: SC apna rules khud bana sakta hai apni internal procedure ke liye (Article 145), President ki manzoori se. Aur ek bahut important baat — SC ke expenses (kharche) 'Consolidated Fund of India' par 'charged' hain — matlab Parliament ko har saal isपर vote karne ki zaroorat nahi hai, ye automatically diya jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Charged expenditure! Ye to President ki salary jaisa hi hai na sir — jo bhi 'charged' hota hai, uspar Parliament vote nahi karti?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi Raju! Ab ek aur bahut powerful concept — 'Contempt of Court' — Article 129 ke anusar SC ek 'Court of Record' hai aur uske paas apna 'Contempt' (avmaanana) punish karne ki power hai. Matlab agar koi SC ki avmaanana kare, to SC khud usse punish kar sakta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Court of Record? Ye kya hota hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'Court of Record' ka matlab hai — SC ke faisle aur proceedings permanent record ke roop mein rakhe jaate hain, aur inhe kisi bhi court mein evidence ke roop mein cite kiya jaa sakta hai — aur inpar kisi ordinary court mein sawaal nahi uthaya jaa sakta. Ye ek bahut important status hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Court of Record — permanent record, questionable nahi. Ye sab mila ke SC ko bahut powerful banata hai independent rehne ke liye!

quiz_payload.question: Article 121 ke anusar Parliament mein SC judge ke conduct par kab discussion ho sakta hai?

options.text: Kabhi bhi ho sakti hai, koi restriction nahi
Sirf removal (impeachment) motion ke process mein hi ho sakti hai
Sirf CJI ki permission se ho sakti hai
President ki manzoori se kabhi bhi ho sakti hai

quiz_payload.explanation: Article 121 ke anusar SC judge ke conduct par Parliament mein discussion sirf tab ho sakta hai jab uske removal ka motion process chal raha ho — ye judicial independence ka ek bada safeguard hai.

quiz_payload.question: Supreme Court ke expenses (kharche) kis fund par 'charged' hote hain?

options.text: Contingency Fund of India
Consolidated Fund of India
Public Account of India

quiz_payload.explanation: Supreme Court ke expenses Consolidated Fund of India par 'charged' hote hain — matlab Parliament ko har saal isपर separately vote karne ki zaroorat nahi, ye automatically diya jaata hai. Ye financial independence ka safeguard hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab dekhte hain Supreme Court asal mein kaam kya karta hai — iski power ko 4 categories mein baanta gaya hai: 1) Original Jurisdiction, 2) Writ Jurisdiction, 3) Appellate Jurisdiction, 4) Advisory Jurisdiction. Chalo pehle Original Jurisdiction se shuru karte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 'Original Jurisdiction' matlab kya hota hai sir? Ye alag kaise hai baaki teen se?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'Original Jurisdiction' matlab wo cases jo SEEDHE SC mein hi file hote hain — kisi lower court se appeal hokar nahi aate, SC hi pehli aur aakhri court hoti hai unke liye. Article 131 iske baare mein hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, seedhe SC mein file hone wale cases! Kaunse cases aise hote hain sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Article 131 ke anusar Original Jurisdiction mein 3 tarah ke disputes aate hain: 1) Union vs ek ya adhik States ke beech dispute, 2) Union aur kisi State(s) ek taraf, aur ek ya adhik dusri States doosri taraf, 3) Do ya adhik States ke beech dispute.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Matlab ye sirf government-to-government disputes hain? Aam nagrik (citizen) apna case yahan file nahi kar sakta?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi pakda! Original Jurisdiction sirf Centre-State ya State-State disputes ke liye hai, jismein koi 'legal right' ka sawaal ho. Private citizen isme party nahi ban sakta. Ye Centre-State ya State-State FEDERAL disputes solve karne ke liye hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, federal disputes ke liye hai ye. Par sir kya har tarah ka Centre-State dispute yahan aa sakta hai, ya koi exceptions bhi hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut zaroori sawaal, aur yahin bada BPSC trap hai! Kuch matters Original Jurisdiction ke DAYRE se BAHAR hain: 1) Inter-State water disputes (Article 262 ke tahat, ye alag tribunal dekhte hain, SC nahi), 2) Kuch treaty/agreement se related matters jo pehle se exclude kiye gaye hon, 3) Finance Commission ke saath related matters.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Inter-State water dispute SC mein nahi jaata?? Ye to bahut common lagta tha mujhe SC ka hi kaam!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yahin trap hai! Article 262 ke tahat Parliament ne 'Inter-State River Water Disputes Act' banaya hai jismein ek alag Tribunal water disputes suljhata hai — SC ka Original Jurisdiction yahan lagu NAHI hota. Ye BPSC mein multiple baar puchha ja chuka hai!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa!! Water dispute = alag Tribunal, SC nahi. Ye ekdum yaad rakhunga sir, warna exam mein confuse ho jaunga!

milestone_payload.motivational_quote: Water dispute wala bada trap crack ho gaya! Ab dekhte hain Fundamental Rights ki raksha kaise hoti hai — Writ Jurisdiction.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, ab ek bahut important Article — Article 32. Ye kehta hai ki agar kisi ke Fundamental Rights ka ullangan (violation) ho, to wo seedhe Supreme Court jaa sakta hai. Dr. Ambedkar ne isse kya kaha tha, guess karo?

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Sir aapne pehle CAG ko 'most important officer' bataya tha — is Article ko bhi kuch bola hoga important?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut sahi! Ambedkar ne Article 32 ko 'The Heart and Soul of the Constitution' kaha tha — matlab agar Constitution ek shareer hai, to ye Article uska dil aur aatma hai. Isliye ki bina isake, Fundamental Rights sirf kagaz par likhi baatein reh jaatin, unhe enforce karwane ka koi tarika nahi hota.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Heart and Soul!! Ye to bahut powerful line hai. To Article 32 khud bhi ek Fundamental Right hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi Raju! Article 32 khud Fundamental Rights ke Part III mein aata hai — matlab 'apne Fundamental Rights ko enforce karwane ka adhikar' bhi khud ek Fundamental Right hai! Ye ek bahut unique double-layer protection hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Wow, right to enforce a right! Achha sir, ye SC mein kaise jaate hain — koi form bharte hain kya?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: SC 'Writs' — yaani likhit aadesh — jaari karta hai Fundamental Rights ki raksha ke liye. Total 5 tarah ke writs hain — Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, aur Quo-Warranto. Ye concept British legal system se liya gaya hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Panch writs! Ye naam to bahut alag-alag hain sir, mix ho jaayenge. Ek-ek karke samjhaiye please!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Pehla writ — 'Habeas Corpus' — Latin mein iska matlab hai 'to have the body' (shareer ko prastut karo). Ye writ tab jaari hoti hai jab kisi ko galat tarike se detain (band) kiya gaya ho — court kehti hai ki uss vyakti ko court ke saamne pesh karo aur bataao kis aadhar par usse rokha hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Matlab agar police kisi ko bina wajah pakad ke rakh le, to Habeas Corpus se usse chhudaya ja sakta hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye illegal detention ke khilaf sabse powerful hathiyaar hai — 'body ko produce karo court mein'. Agar detention illegal nikle, court turant release karne ka order de sakti hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Habeas Corpus — illegal detention ke khilaf. Yaad ho gaya sir! Agla kaunsa hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Doosra writ — 'Mandamus' — Latin mein matlab 'We command' (hum aadesh dete hain). Ye writ tab jaari hoti hai jab koi public official ya government body apna duty (kaam) nahi kar rahi ho jo unhe karna chahiye tha — court unhe order deti hai ki apna kartavya poora karo.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Matlab agar koi sarkari afsar apna kaam nahi kar raha to Mandamus se usse force kiya ja sakta hai kaam karne ke liye?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Lekin ek important exception yaad rakho — Mandamus President ya Governor ke khilaf jaari nahi ki jaa sakti, aur na hi kisi private individual ya company ke khilaf (jab tak wo public duty na perform kar rahi ho).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: President-Governor ke khilaf nahi! Ye exception yaad rakhunga. Ab teesra batao sir.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Teesra — 'Prohibition' — matlab 'to forbid' (rokna). Ye ek higher court se lower court/tribunal ko jaari hoti hai jab wo apni jurisdiction se BAAHAR jaakar kaam kar rahi ho — court kehti hai 'ruk jaao, tumhare pass ye adhikar hi nahi hai'. Ye PREVENTIVE hai — kaam hone se pehle rokti hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Preventive! Matlab kaam hone se pehle roka jaata hai. Aur chautha writ?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Chautha — 'Certiorari' — matlab 'to be certified' ya 'to be informed'. Ye bhi lower court/tribunal ke jurisdiction ke bahar jaane par jaari hoti hai, LEKIN ye CURATIVE hai — jab kaam ho CHUKA ho, tab uss faisle ko higher court apne yahan transfer karke cancel/quash kar deti hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Prohibition = pehle rokna (preventive), Certiorari = ho chuke kaam ko cancel karna (curative). Ye dono bahut similar lag rahe the, ab fark samajh aaya sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Paanchwa aur aakhri writ — 'Quo-Warranto' — Latin mein matlab 'by what authority/warrant' (kis adhikar se). Ye tab jaari hoti hai jab koi vyakti kisi PUBLIC OFFICE (sarkari pad) par baitha ho jispar baithne ka usse koi kanooni adhikar (legal right) na ho.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Matlab agar koi bina qualification ke kisi bade pad par baith jaaye, to Quo-Warranto se usse challenge kiya ja sakta hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Aur ek important note — Quo-Warranto sirf PUBLIC office ke liye hai, PRIVATE ya company ke office ke liye nahi. Aur interesting baat — Quo-Warranto ek aisi writ hai jo koi bhi interested citizen file kar sakta hai, sirf 'affected party' hona zaroori nahi hai — baaki 4 writs mein aam taur par 'affected party' hi file karti hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achhaaaa! Quo-Warranto special hai — koi bhi file kar sakta hai! Ye interesting exception hai, likh liya maine sir.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab ek bahut important comparison — High Courts bhi writs jaari kar sakte hain, Article 226 ke tahat. Par yahan ek bada fark hai — SC (Article 32) sirf FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS ke violation ke liye writ jaari kar sakta hai. High Court (Article 226) Fundamental Rights KE SAATH-SAATH 'any other purpose' (matlab koi bhi legal right) ke liye bhi writ jaari kar sakta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Matlab High Court ki writ power SC se bhi zyada wide hai?? Ye to bahut bada trap hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye ek bahut famous PYQ trap hai — 'High Court ki writ jurisdiction, SC se WIDER hai' (matlab jyada cheezon ko cover karti hai), lekin High Court ki writ SIRF apne territorial jurisdiction (uss State/UT) tak seemित hai, jabki SC ki writ poore desh mein applicable hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! HC ki power wider hai matlab (fundamental rights + koi bhi legal right), par sirf apne state mein. SC ki power narrower hai (sirf fundamental rights), par poore desh mein. Ye balance samajh aaya sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab dekhte hain Supreme Court ka SABSE zyada use hone wala jurisdiction — 'Appellate Jurisdiction'. Ye woh cases hain jinme koi lower court (High Court) ke faisle ke khilaf log SC mein 'appeal' (punarvichaar ki maang) karte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, ye to humne shuru mein hi discuss kiya tha na sir — jab humne panchayat ka example liya tha?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi याद rakha! Appellate Jurisdiction ko 4 categories mein baanta gaya hai: 1) Constitutional matters (Article 132), 2) Civil matters (Article 133), 3) Criminal matters (Article 134), aur 4) Special Leave Petition — SLP (Article 136).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Char categories! Special Leave Petition ka naam suna hai maine news mein — ye kya hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Pehle baaki teen samajh lein — Article 132 (Constitutional matters): agar HC certify kare ki case mein Constitution ki 'substantial interpretation' ka sawaal hai, to seedhe SC mein appeal ho sakti hai — chahe wo civil ho ya criminal ya koi bhi matter.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, matlab agar Constitution ki interpretation ka bada sawaal ho to appeal ho sakti hai. Aur Civil-Criminal ka fark kya hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Article 133 (Civil matters): HC certify kare ki case mein 'general importance ka substantial sawaal' hai, to civil case mein SC appeal ho sakti hai. Article 134 (Criminal matters): agar HC ne kisi ko acquittal se convert karke death sentence diya ho, ya HC ne khud kisi case ko SC ke liye 'fit' certify kiya ho, tab hi criminal appeal SC mein ho sakti hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, Constitution = interpretation sawaal, Civil = general importance sawaal, Criminal = death sentence ya HC certify kare. Teenon mein 'HC certificate' zaroori lagta hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut sahi observation Raju! Article 132, 133, 134 — teenon mein HC ka certificate zaroori hai. Lekin ab Article 136 — 'Special Leave Petition (SLP)' — ye ek EXTRAORDINARY power hai jismein SC KHUD, apni marzi se, bina kisi certificate ke, kisi bhi court ya tribunal (Court Martial ko chhodkar) ke kisi bhi faisle ke khilaf appeal sunne ki permission (special leave) de sakta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! SLP mein HC ka certificate zaroori nahi hai? SC khud hi decide karta hai ki sunna hai ya nahi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye SC ki 'discretionary' power hai — SC chahe to case sune, chahe to na sune. Isliye SLP ko 'residuary power' bhi kaha jaata hai — jahan aur koi appeal ka raasta nahi hai, wahan SLP ek aakhri umeed ban sakti hai. Bas ek exception yaad rakho — Court Martial (military courts) ke faisle ke khilaf SLP NAHI file ki jaa sakti.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Court Martial exception! Ye important hai. SLP to bahut powerful lag raha hai sir — 'kisi bhi court ke khilaf'!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab aakhri jurisdiction — 'Advisory Jurisdiction' — Article 143 ke tahat. Ye kehta hai ki agar President ko lagta hai ki koi 'law' ya 'fact' ka sawaal itna important hai ki public interest mein SC ki opinion leni chahiye, to President SC se salaah maang sakte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! To President SC se salaah maang sakte hain? Kya SC ko wo salaah deni HI padegi?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut zaroori trap yahan hai! Article 143(1) ke matters mein SC 'may' report kare — matlab SC chahe to opinion de sakta hai, ya mana bhi kar sakta hai (discretionary). Lekin ek doosri category hai Article 143(2) — jo pre-Constitution treaties se related hai — usme SC ko OPINION DENI HI PADEGI, mandatory hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Ek discretionary, ek mandatory! Ye do categories bhi yaad rakhni hongi. Aur ye advisory opinion binding hoti hai kya President ke liye?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bahut important sawaal, aur yahan sabse bada trap hai! Advisory opinion (Article 143 ke tahat) President par BINDING NAHI hoti — President chahe to accept karein, chahe to reject kar dein! Ye SC ke normal judicial faislon se bilkul alag hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? SC opinion de aur President use maane hi na?? Ye to bahut ajeeb lagta hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi observation, isiliye ye baar-baar poocha jaata hai! Yaad rakho — Article 143 mein SC 'advise' karta hai, order nahi deta. Ek real example — Ayodhya Ram Janmabhoomi case (1994, Ismail Faruqui case) mein President ne SC se advisory opinion mangi thi, lekin SC ne opinion dene se MANA kar diya tha kyunki wo purely religious sawaal tha.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: SC ne mana bhi kiya kabhi opinion dene se! Ye to bahut interesting fact hai sir — advisory power discretionary hone ka matlab hi ye hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, yaad hai Module 2 mein humne kaha tha ki judges ki niyukti mein 'consultation' hoti hai? Ab detail mein samjhte hain — is consultation ka matlab kya hai iske liye 3 famous Supreme Court cases hue, unhe 'Three Judges Cases' kaha jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Teen cases? Ye kya hua tha inme sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: First Judges Case (1981, S.P. Gupta case) mein SC ne kaha ki 'consultation' ka matlab sirf salaah lena hai, President (matlab executive/government) ki final decision maanni zaroori nahi. Isse government ko judges appointment mein zyada power mili.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, pehle case mein sarkar ki hi chalti thi? Phir kya badla?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Second Judges Case (1993) mein SC ne apni hi 1981 wali baat palat di! Ab kaha gaya ki 'consultation' ka matlab hai 'concurrence' — matlab CJI ki salaah ko MAANNA zaroori hai. Isi case se 'Collegium System' ka janam hua.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Collegium — ye naam suna hai maine news mein bahut! Ye kya hota hai exactly sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'Collegium' matlab CJI + kuch senior-most SC judges ka ek group, jo judges ki niyukti aur transfer ka faisla lete hain. 1993 mein ye CJI + 2 senior-most judges ka group tha. Third Judges Case (1998) mein isse aur expand karke CJI + 4 senior-most judges kar diya gaya — jo aaj bhi lagu hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Teen cases ka effect — 1981 government wins, 1993 judiciary wins (Collegium banta hai), 1998 Collegium expand hota hai. Interesting evolution hai ye sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Aaj ki tarikh mein Supreme Court Collegium mein CJI + 4 senior-most SC judges hote hain — total 5 log. Ye group milkar decide karta hai ki kaun SC judge banega, kaun High Court Chief Justice banega, aur judges ka transfer kaise hoga.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 5 log — CJI + 4 senior judges. Aur ye Collegium Constitution mein likha hai kya sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yahin sabse bada trap hai Raju! Collegium System Constitution mein KAHIN bhi LIKHA HUA NAHI hai! Ye poori tarah SC ke apne judgements (1993, 1998 wale cases) se banaya gaya system hai — ise 'judge-made law' bhi kaha jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Hain?? Itna important system Constitution mein likha hi nahi hai?? Ye to seriously bahut bada trap hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Ab ek recent aur bahut important development — Parliament ne 2014 mein 99th Constitutional Amendment Act pass kiya jisse 'National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)' banaya gaya, jo Collegium system ko replace karne wala tha.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: NJAC kaise different tha Collegium se sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: NJAC mein CJI + 2 senior SC judges + Law Minister + 2 'eminent persons' (jo PM, CJI, Leader of Opposition select karte) hote — matlab executive ka bhi seedha role hota judges appointment mein. Lekin ye ek bahut bada twist le kar aaya!

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Kya hua sir? Lagu ho gaya kya NJAC?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Yahin sabse bada twist hai! Supreme Court ne khud, 'Fourth Judges Case (2015)' mein, 99th Amendment aur NJAC Act ko UNCONSTITUTIONAL declare kar diya! SC ne kaha ki isse 'judicial independence' ko khatra hai, jo Basic Structure ka hissa hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: SC ne Parliament ke banaye Amendment ko hi khaarij kar diya?? Ye to bahut bada power hai SC ke paas!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Isi wajah se aaj bhi purana Collegium System hi chal raha hai, NJAC kabhi implement nahi ho paya. Ye ek zabardast example hai ki kaise 'Judicial Independence' Basic Structure ka part hai jise Parliament bhi nahi badal sakti.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Judicial Independence = Basic Structure! Ye bahut important connection hai — Kesavananda Bharati wale Basic Structure se link ho gaya ye to!

milestone_payload.motivational_quote: 4 Judges Cases ki poori kahani yaad ho gaya! Ab Judicial Review, PIL aur landmark cases dekhte hain.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, ek bahut powerful concept — 'Judicial Review'. Ye SC (aur HC) ki power hai jismein wo kisi bhi kanoon (Parliament ya State Legislature ka banaya) ya executive action ko Constitution ke against paakar 'unconstitutional' declare kar sakte hain.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Matlab SC, Parliament ke banaye kanoon ko bhi cancel kar sakta hai?? Ye to bahut bada power hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Ye humne abhi NJAC case mein bhi dekha. 'Judicial Review' explicit roop mein kisi ek article mein 'likha hua' nahi hai, lekin ye kai Articles se implied hai — Article 13, 32, 226, aur 245 se derive hota hai. Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) mein SC ne Judicial Review ko Basic Structure ka part bhi declare kiya.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, Judicial Review bhi Basic Structure hai! Kesavananda Bharati case ke baare mein aur bataiye sir, ye bahut famous naam hai.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala (1973) India ka sabse landmark case maana jaata hai! Ye 13-judge bench ne (sabse bada bench aaj tak) decide kiya ki Parliament Constitution mein amendment to kar sakti hai (Article 368 se), LEKIN uska 'Basic Structure' (buniyaadi dhaancha) nahi badal sakti.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 13-judge bench!! Itna bada bench? Aur 'Basic Structure' mein kya-kya aata hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Basic Structure mein Supremacy of Constitution, Rule of Law, Judicial Review, Separation of Powers, Federalism, Secularism, Democracy — jaise core principles aate hain. Isse pehle Golaknath case (1967) mein SC ne kaha tha ki Parliament Fundamental Rights ko BILKUL bhi amend nahi kar sakti — Kesavananda ne isse thoda balance kiya.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Golaknath — bilkul nahi, Kesavananda — Basic Structure chhodkar sab kuch amend kar sakte hain. Interesting evolution hai! Aur koi important case hai sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan, do aur bahut important cases yaad karo — Minerva Mills case (1980) — isme SC ne kaha ki 'Judicial Review' khud Basic Structure ka part hai, aur Fundamental Rights aur Directive Principles ke beech 'harmony aur balance' bhi Basic Structure ka hissa hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Aur ek aur case bola tha aapne — Maneka Gandhi wala?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India (1978) — is case ne Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) ki interpretation ko poori tarah badal diya. Ab 'procedure established by law' ko 'fair, just aur reasonable' hona zaroori maana gaya — isse Article 21 ka daayra bahut expand ho gaya.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Maneka Gandhi case se Article 21 bahut wide ho gaya. Sir, ab PIL ke baare mein bhi bataiye — ye bhi bahut suna hai maine.

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'Public Interest Litigation (PIL)' ek bahut zaroori concept hai — normally court mein case wahi vyakti file kar sakta hai jiske apne rights affect hue hon ('locus standi' rule). PIL ne is rule ko relax kiya — ab koi bhi public-spirited citizen, kisi aur ke ya samaaj ke behalf par bhi case file kar sakta hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Matlab agar mujhe pata chale ki kisi gaanv mein bacchon ko school nahi mil raha, to main khud unki taraf se case file kar sakta hoon?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi udaharan! PIL ka credit Justice P.N. Bhagwati aur Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer ko diya jaata hai — unhone 1980s mein 'Judicial Activism' ke through PIL ko promote kiya, taaki gareeb aur weaker sections ko bhi justice mil sake, chahe wo khud court na aa payein.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Judicial Activism! Ye bhi naya term hai sir — kya matlab hai iska?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: 'Judicial Activism' matlab jab court proactive roop se, sirf case sunne tak limited na rehkar, samaaj ke faayde ke liye policy-jaise directions bhi de — jaise environment protection, human rights, corruption ke khilaf action. Isse SC ko kai baar 'activist' ya proactive maana jaata hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! To SC sirf case sunta nahi, active roop se samaaj ke liye kaam bhi karta hai. Iski koi criticism bhi hoti hai kya sir?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Haan, critics kehte hain ki excessive Judicial Activism 'Separation of Powers' ko todता hai — kyunki policy-making ka kaam Legislature/Executive ka hota hai, judiciary ka nahi. Isse 'Judicial Overreach' bhi kaha jaata hai jab court apni limit paar kar de.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, Judicial Activism achha bhi hai, par overreach bura hai. Ye balance samajh mein aaya sir. Ab Bihar-specific kuch batao please!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: ⭐ BPSC TRE Favorite: Bihar mein 'Patna High Court' hai, jo 1916 mein sthapित (established) hui thi — ye Bihar ki apni High Court hai jiske faisle ke khilaf appeal SC mein hoti hai. Article 214 ke tahat har state ki High Court hoti hai, aur Bihar ke liye ye Patna High Court hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: 1916 mein bani thi Patna High Court? Ye to Independence se bhi pehle ki baat hai sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Patna High Court, Calcutta High Court se alag hokar bani thi jab Bihar aur Orissa ko ek naya province banaya gaya tha. Aur ek zaroori fact — Bihar ke saath Supreme Court judges mein bhi kai important naam hain jinka Bihar se sambandh raha hai — jaise Justice Ramaswami sir (jo Patna High Court se bhi jude the SC judge banne se pehle).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Patna HC 1916 se hai. Ye BPSC mein zaroor puchhа jaayega, ab yaad ho gaya sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Raju, ek aakhri bahut zaroori Article — Article 141. Ye kehta hai ki SC dwara 'declared law' desh ke saare courts par BINDING hoga — matlab jo bhi SC decide kare, sab courts (High Courts, District Courts) ko wahi follow karna hoga.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Matlab SC ka faisla ek precedent (mstandard) ban jaata hai jo sab courts follow karti hain?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi! Isse 'Doctrine of Precedent' bhi kehte hain — 'stare decisis' ka principle. Lekin ek zaroori note — SC khud apne pichhle faisle se bandhа nahi hota, wo apni hi larger bench se pichle faisle ko overrule kar sakta hai (jaise humne dekha Golaknath ko Kesavananda ne partially overrule kiya).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha! Sab courts SC follow karte hain, par SC khud apna faisla badal sakta hai bade bench se. Ye samajh gaya sir!

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Kuch aakhri trivia facts yaad karte hain — India ke pehle Chief Justice of India the Justice H.J. Kania (1950-51). CJI ki niyukti mein ek convention follow hota hai — 'seniority principle' — matlab senior-most judge hi agla CJI banta hai (halaanki ye Constitution mein likha nahi hai, ek parampara hai).

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Seniority se CJI banta hai? Ye bhi Collegium jaisa hi hai — Constitution mein likha nahi, par follow hota hai?

messages.speaker: aman
messages.text: Bilkul sahi observation! Halaanki 1973 aur 1977 mein iss convention ko todkar junior judges ko CJI banaya gaya tha (superseding senior judges) — jo bahut controversial hua tha. Uske baad se seniority principle strictly follow hota hai.

messages.speaker: raju
messages.text: Achha, 1973-77 mein exception hua tha! Interesting history hai ye. Ab last module ka revision karte hain sir!

summary_payload.title: ⚡ Officer Revision — Supreme Court ka Poora Nichod

revision_points.point: Article 124-147 (Part V, Chapter IV). Established 28 Jan 1950 (Federal Court replace kiya). Strength: 1950 mein 8 (1 CJI+7), abhi 34 (1 CJI+33, 2019 se). Qualification: 5 saal HC judge, YA 10 saal HC advocate, YA Distinguished Jurist — koi minimum age nahi. Retirement age: 65 saal.

Removal = SC judge jaisi process — dono sadan mein SAME session mein special majority (total membership majority + 2/3rd present-voting), proved misbehaviour/incapacity ground. Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968 — 3-member committee pehle janch karti hai. Aaj tak koi judge successfully removed nahi hua (Justice Ramaswami 1993 bach gaye).

Original (Art 131) — Centre-State/State-State disputes, water disputes EXCLUDE. Writ (Art 32) — 5 writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo-Warranto — sirf Fundamental Rights ke liye (HC ki Art 226 power wider hai par territorial). Appellate (Art 132-136) — SLP (Art 136) sabse powerful, Court Martial exclude. Advisory (Art 143) — non-binding on President.

First Judges Case (1981) — consultation = salaah lena. Second Judges Case (1993) — consultation = concurrence, Collegium janma (CJI+2). Third Judges Case (1998) — Collegium CJI+4 hua. NJAC (99th Amendment 2014) — Fourth Judges Case (2015) mein unconstitutional declare hua, Collegium hi chalta hai. Collegium Constitution mein LIKHA HUA NAHI hai.

Kesavananda Bharati (1973, 13-judge bench) — Basic Structure Doctrine. Golaknath (1967), Minerva Mills (1980) — Judicial Review = Basic Structure. Maneka Gandhi (1978) — Article 21 expand. Article 141 — SC ka law sab courts par binding. Patna High Court sthापित 1916 mein, Bihar ki apni High Court.
